shortDescription: Mexican financial group Kapital said on Wednesday it had raised $125 million in financing to invest in its AI platform and to support expansion in priority markets.

children: Mexican financial group Kapital said on Wednesday it had raised $125 million in financing to invest in its AI platform and to support expansion in priority markets.

Mexico City-based Kapital provides loans, deposit accounts, foreign-exchange services and other products to businesses, mainly small and medium-sized firms. The company operates in Mexico, Colombia, Spain and the U.S.
Kapital also offers an AI-led software tool for clients to forecast sales, track cash flow and monitor costs.
The financing was led by Tru Arrow Partners and Fasanara Capital, with Cervin Ventures, Niya Partners and Overlook Capital also joining.

The deal ranks among the larger fintech fundraisings in the region in the past year, and is part of Kapital's push to becoming a broader financial group. In 2023, Kapital bought Mexican bank Autofin to sidestep the lengthy process of independently applying for a banking license.
"This new capital will enable us to accelerate our next stage of growth and expand our impact in priority markets such as Mexico and the United States," Kapital CEO Rene Saul said.
Last year, Kapital's valuation topped $1 billion, making it a so-called "unicorn."
Kapital said its loan portfolio exceeded $1.7 billion in the first half of 2026, more than tripling from a year earlier.
